title: The crane that lost its flock
takeaway: The cleverest minds in history lost to love. Don't think you're the exception.
scene: The beloved promised to come back soon, and never did. The poet waits through endless nights, and compares himself to a crane that has lost its flock.

original: سجناں بوہڑ شتابی دل دیاں پیاں کہن تراٹاں
ساہاں والیاں مک چلیاں نے ہن تے ساریاں واٹاں
transliteration: Sajnaan bauhar shitaabi, dil diyaan piyaan kehan traataan
Saahaan vaaliyaan mukk chaliyaan ne hun te saariyaan vaataan
translation: 'Come back quickly, my love,' cry the aches of my heart.
The road of my breaths is almost at its end.
couplets.story: His heart is crying out: please come back, and hurry. He feels like he is running out of breath, as if his life is nearly over and there isn't much time left.

original: بخت میرے دی کالکھ خورے کیوں اجے نئیں لتھی
جگ نوں کر منور گئیاں حسن تیرے دیاں لاٹاں
transliteration: Bakht mere di kaalakh khoore kyon ajje nahin latthi
Jag nu kar munavvar gaiyaan husn tere diyaan laataan
translation: Who knows why the darkness of my fate still hasn't lifted,
when the flames of your beauty have lit up the whole world.
couplets.story: The beloved's beauty shines so bright it lights up the whole world. So why is his own life still so dark? He can't work it out.

original: وچ محلاں بہہ کے سوہنا بھل گیا اوہ سارے
جیہڑے قول قرار سی کیتے بہہ کے وچ پلاٹاں
transliteration: Vich mehlaan beh ke sohna bhul gaya oh saare
Jehre qaul qaraar si keete beh ke vich plaataan
translation: Sitting in palaces now, my lovely one has forgotten
all the promises we made sitting together out in the fields.
couplets.story: Back when they were both simple people, sitting together in the fields, the beloved made him promises. Now the beloved lives in a palace and has forgotten every one of them.

original: لالچ لوبھ نوں ہتھ نہ پاندے مونہہ شراب نہ لاندے
جنہاں رنداں تائیں لگیاں حسن تیرے دیاں چاٹاں
transliteration: Laalach lobh nu hatth na paande, moonh sharaab na laande
Jinhaan rindaan taaeen lagiyaan husn tere diyaan chaataan
translation: They don't lay a hand on greed, or put wine to their lips,
those free spirits who've got a taste for your beauty.
couplets.story: Once someone has tasted the beloved's beauty, ordinary pleasures stop tempting them. They don't care about money anymore, and they don't need alcohol. They're already 'drunk' on something better.

original: ہتھ رقیباں ایسے آئے جان ہوئی زچ میری
بھنڈیا وچ زمانے سارے مینوں میریاں کاتاں
transliteration: Hatth raqeebaan aise aaye, jaan hoi zich meri
Bhandiya vich zamaane saare mainu meriyaan kaataan
translation: I fell into my rivals' hands so badly my life was made miserable.
My own letters disgraced me in front of the whole world.
couplets.story: His rivals got hold of him and made his life miserable. Worse, the love letters he wrote got out, and now the whole world is gossiping about him.

original: نبضاں تیز ہو جاون میرے کول جدوں آہندے
دور ہون تے ہجراں مارے دل نوں ہندیاں گھاتاں
transliteration: Nabzaan tez ho jaavan mere kol jadon aande
Door hon te hijraan maare dil nu hundiyaan ghaataan
translation: My pulse races whenever they come near me,
and when they're far, my lovesick heart is ambushed with pain.
couplets.story: When the beloved comes close, his heart starts racing. When they leave, pain jumps on his lonely heart like an ambush.

original: ہجر وچھنا درد تیرے وچ کیوں نہ دئے دوہائی
وچھڑ جائے کونج جوڑاروں پاندی اے کرلاٹاں
transliteration: Hijr vichhuna dard tere vich kyon na de duhaai
Vichhar jaaye koonj jodaaron paandi ae karlaataan
translation: Separated from you, why shouldn't I cry out in pain?
When a crane is cut off from its flock, it cries and cries.
couplets.story: Of course he cries out. Think of a crane that has lost its flock in the sky. It calls and calls, looking for the others. That's what he's like without the beloved.

original: افلاطون ارسطو ورگے ایتھے ہار گئے نیں
عشق دا رنگ جنہاں نوں لگے دار و کرن نہ کاتاں
transliteration: Aflaatoon Arastoo varge ethe haar gaye nain
Ishq da rang jinhaan nu lagge, daar o karan na kaataan
translation: Even the likes of Plato and Aristotle were defeated here.
Those who are dyed in love's colour don't fear the gallows.
couplets.story: Even the smartest people in history, like the Greek thinkers Plato and Aristotle, lost when it came to love. And once someone is 'dyed' in love, they aren't scared of anything, not even being hanged for it.

original: آکھن والے کہندے رہ گئے احمدؔ دل سنبھالیں
کھوون والے کھوہ لے جاندے پل وچ مار چراٹاں
transliteration: Aakhan vaale kehnde reh gaye Ahmad dil sambhaaleen
Khohan vaale khoh lai jaande pal vich maar chraataan
translation: People kept telling me, 'Ahmad, guard your heart!'
But those who steal hearts snatch them in an instant, with one swift glance.
couplets.story: Everyone warned him: be careful with your heart, Ahmad. It didn't help. The person who steals a heart takes it in a second, with a single look.

deeper:
The koonj, a crane separated from its flock, is one of the great Punjabi images for the soul. Mystics like Bulleh Shah and Sultan Bahu use it for the soul cut off from God, its true home, and calling out to return.

Some 'free spirits' lose interest in greed and wine once they've tasted the Beloved's beauty. That is how real love for God works: it changes what you want, from the inside. And Plato and Aristotle losing to love is the Sufi claim that the mind, however brilliant, cannot reach God on its own. The heart has to be 'dyed in love's colour'.

'The flames of your beauty have lit up the whole world' can also be heard as praise of the Prophet ﷺ, whom the Qur'an calls 'a lamp giving light' (33:46). The poem doesn't name him, so this is only a possible reading.
why: The crane image is famous in Punjabi culture, so this poem is a good way into that whole tradition of longing.
prompt: Have you ever felt like the crane, cut off from where or who you belong with?
notes: Couplet 5: 'kaataan' is read as 'letters' (from 'khat'); it may instead mean 'cuts/wounds'.
